why: Both say to keep the container name and use the container port 27017 instead of the published one, which is exactly the confirmed fix.

The service ran on the host, and both say to use host.docker.internal instead of localhost (adding host-gateway on Engine), the change that fixed the connection; the image swap and dropping sshd in the container were incidental.
The tool named no cause and gave no fix.

The target was another container (container_2:8000), but both send the client to host.docker.internal on the condition that the service runs on the host. They never name container_2 or its container port.
Both say ki-backend:8000 instead of localhost:8000, the same proxy_pass change. Restarting nginx is just how the change is applied.
Both say to call the API through the port files-service publishes on localhost, which is the confirmed fix (the lab's port stands in for 6060).

Both correctly find that the MySQL container had stopped and point to its logs, where the cause would show. But starting it alone would not help: the needed config change (MYSQL_USER not root, and the 3306 port) is missing.
Authentik ran in containers on another Compose network. The fix was to join that network and use the server's container name, but both point at a host service via host.docker.internal.
Both say db:5432 instead of the published port, the confirmed fix.
Both say consul:8500 instead of localhost:8500. That is what setting consul.host to CONSUL_HOST=consul did.
Both say to publish the Redis port with -p (or Compose ports), the confirmed fix in substance. Binding to all interfaces rather than 127.0.0.1 is a detail.

Both cover publishing kafka-1's port but miss the second needed part: the host listener advertised as localhost. Without it the Kafka client still gets the internal kafka-1:29092 address after bootstrap. They also do not mention the other brokers.
Both say to use the postgres service name instead of localhost, exactly what was entered in pgAdmin.

The right change (the Compose service name instead of localhost) is offered next to a host.docker.internal alternative, without saying which applies. Neither names the api service or its port 5000 (the tool's text keeps 5001).
The fix was to make the primary service itself listen on 9200 (--api-port 9200). Both say to point the client at another container or the host instead, which would not create the missing listener.
